Full reference

swiftlet.simulation_suites.get_suite(suite)[source]

Returns SimulationSuite for a pre-defined swift simulation suite (e.g. “flamingo” or “colibre”).

Parameters:

suite (str or SimulationSuite) – name of the suite, or a SimulationSuite

swiftlet.simulation_suites.output_redshifts(boxsize_resolution, simulation_suite_name=None)[source]

Return the stored output redshifts for a SWIFT simulation.

Output redshifts of the snapshots of a box size and resolution, as read from its snapshot number - redshift tables, for when only the redshifts are needed (otherwise use Simulation.output_redshifts).

Returns an np.ndarray, in order of snapshot number.

Parameters:

  • boxsize_resolution (str) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800” (FLAMINGO) or “L0200N1504” (COLIBRE)

  • simulation_suite_name (str) – “flamingo” or “colibre”. If None, found from boxsize_resolution

swiftlet.simulation_suites.read_output_redshifts(path)[source]

Read snapshot redshifts from .yml files.

Read the output redshifts of a simulation’s snapshots from a text file of comma separated values, one snapshot per line, “snapshot_number, redshift”, with the snapshot numbers 0, 1, 2, … in order. Lines starting with ‘#’ are comments.

Returns an np.ndarray of the redshifts, in order of snapshot number.

Parameters:

path (str or os.PathLike) – a file name, for the tables shipped with the package (in OUTPUT_REDSHIFT_DIR), or the path of a file of your own

swiftlet.simulation_suites.suite_for_label(boxsize_resolution=None, simulation_suite_name=None)[source]

Identify the simulation suite from a simultations label.

The suite is either given as a parameter, or recognised by matching labels with the boxsize_resolution. Raises ValueError if the suite can’t be found, or if the named suite and the label’s disagree.

Parameters:

  • boxsize_resolution (str) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800” (FLAMINGO) or “L0200N1504” (COLIBRE)

  • simulation_suite_name (str or SimulationSuite) – “flamingo” or “colibre” (or a SimulationSuite). If None, found from boxsize_resolution

swiftlet.simulation_suites.write_output_redshifts(filename, redshifts, description=None, **header)[source]

Write the snapshot redshifts to .yml files.

Write the output redshifts of a simulation’s snapshots to a YAML file, one row per snapshot [snapshot_number, redshift]. The redshifts are written so they read back exactly.

Parameters:

  • filename (str or os.PathLike) – path of the .yaml file to write

  • redshifts (array-like of float) – redshift of each snapshot, in order of snapshot number 0, 1, 2, …

  • description (str) – what the redshifts are, e.g. the simulations they are for

  • header – more to write before the rows, e.g. suite=”colibre”

class swiftlet.simulation_suites.Simulation(suite: SimulationSuite, box_res: str, name: str, directory: str)[source]

Bases: object

For one simulation: its suite name, box size and resolution str, model name and base directory.

For every simulation used, every path to a snapshot and every snapshot number - redshift conversion comes from this class. This class allows for consistent use of snapshot number - redshift conversions and pathing for a swift simulation suite

Parameters:

  • suite (SimulationSuite) – the simulation’s suite, FLAMINGO or COLIBRE

  • box_res (str) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800”

  • name (str) – name of the simulation, e.g. “HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”

  • directory (str) – directory of the simulation

box_res: str
name: str
directory: str
classmethod from_label(boxsize_resolution, simulation_name, simulation_suite_name=None, base_dir_format=None)[source]

Get a simulation suite name from its box size and resolution str and name.

Parameters:

  • boxsize_resolution (str) – box size and resolution label, e.g. “L1000N1800” (FLAMINGO) or “L0200N1504” (COLIBRE)

  • simulation_name (str) – name of the simulation, e.g. “HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”

  • simulation_suite (str or SimulationSuite) – “flamingo” or “colibre” (or a SimulationSuite). If None, found from boxsize_resolution

  • base_dir_format (str) – directory of the simulation, with {box_res} and {sim_name} fields. If None, the suite’s directory, see SimulationSuite.directory_format

classmethod from_path(path, simulation_suite_name=None)[source]

Returns the paths for a simulation.

Get a simulation from its directory, <…>/<box_res>/<sim_name>, e.g. “/cosma8/data/dp004/flamingo/Runs/L1000N1800/HYDRO_FIDUCIAL”. The suite is found from the box size and resolution label, or from “flamingo” or “colibre” in the path.

Parameters:

  • path (str) – directory of the simulation

  • simulation_suite_name (str or SimulationSuite) – “flamingo” or “colibre” (or a SimulationSuite). If None, found from the path

class swiftlet.simulation_suites.SimulationSuite(name: str, label_pattern: str, base_dir_format: str, base_dir_env: str, snapshot_format: str, output_redshift_tables: dict)[source]

Bases: object

Class to contain SWIFT simulation suites (i.e. FLAMINGO and COLIBRE) and handle what differs between them.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – “flamingo” or “colibre”

  • base_dir_format (str) – directory of a simulation, with {box_res} and {sim_name} fields

  • base_dir_env (str) – environment variable that, if set, replaces the directory holding the simulation

  • snapshot_format (str) – snapshot file, relative to the simulation’s directory, with {snap_nr} and {file_nr} fields

  • output_redshift_tables – file of the output redshifts of the snapshots (see read_output_redshifts), for each box size and resolution label; the file under “*” is used for any label of the suite

directory_format()[source]

Base directory of a simulation.

Returns a str of the formatted path to the simulations base directory.

Formatted path contains {box_res} and {sim_name} fields: from the suite’s environment variable if set, otherwise base_dir_format.
